findings.reason: The protected source is the robust integer form of the canonical information-capacity solution: it counts observable states per pig and multiplies capacity until every bucket has a distinct outcome vector. It avoids floating-point boundary errors, is concise and conventional, and is already expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 458 and its three-integer Python contract. The O(log buckets) time and O(1) space manifest claims match geometric capacity growth by at least two and three scalar variables; source bounds guarantee at least one complete testing round.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064935660. Its complete-round division, added survivor state, zero-pig initial capacity, strict capacity loop, multiplicative update, pig increment, and returned count are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The binary-outcome bucket counts 50, 200, and 800 span 16x and require 6, 8, and 10 capacity multiplications respectively. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.01x the reference runtime. A correct comparator that explicitly materializes each outcome signature passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 40.74x.

The Approach exactly derives the protected target from complete rounds, death-or-survival states, Cartesian state vectors, and the smallest sufficient exponent. It explains both the constructive bucket coding and the information-theoretic lower bound, then accurately states the integer-loop complexity and all relevant rounding and boundary traps.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It restores the full choose/feed/wait/observe/repeat protocol, both exact source examples, every four-way first-round outcome, the second example's conditional second round, both constraints, and the requirement to identify the poison within the allotted time. The unsupported legacy 1000-bucket example was removed.
